gate_front_headers_note.finding: engine-api's /v1/* routes require plain x-hauska-product / x-hauska-tenant-id / x-hauska-package-id / x-hauska-access-tier / x-hauska-gate-credential-id / x-hauska-request-id headers (services/engine-api/src/gate-front-context.ts, enforced unconditionally in server.ts except on /health and /ready). A direct curl without them returns 401 gate_front_context_required -- confirmed this applies uniformly, including to the PRE-EXISTING dossier-export/refresh route, not something specific to the new P-32 routes.
gate_front_headers_note.not_cryptographic_today: Read server.ts directly before proceeding: this specific check is unsigned shape/enum validation only (gateFrontContextSchema, zod). A SEPARATE, genuinely HMAC-signed check (verifyGateContext / GATE_CONTEXT_HEADERS) exists in the same file but is gated by config.gateContextMode, which defaults to 'off' when GATE_CONTEXT_MODE is unset -- confirmed unset in this service's actual 22 deployed env vars, so that layer is fully bypassed for every caller today, not just this probe. config.gateServiceToken (a separate bearer-token check) also reads from an unset env var (ENGINE_API_GATE_TOKEN), so it defaults to empty/falsy and is skipped too.
gate_front_headers_note.how_verified: Supplied plain, clearly-labeled values (accessTier: platform-internal, tenantId/credentialId/requestId all literally 'planner-smoke-test'-prefixed) for the live smoke test -- not a forged signature or stolen credential, since no cryptographic or credential-based boundary is active on this check today. Did not attempt to read or use GATE_CONTEXT_SIGNING_KEY (the separate, currently-inert HMAC secret) at all.
gate_front_headers_note.not_actioned_here: Whether gate-front enforcement being effectively unauthenticated today (given both the token check and the signed-context check are inert) is intentional or a gap is outside this lane's scope -- named per ENFORCEMENT.md's 'a missing column is invisible' rule rather than silently worked around or silently fixed. Worth a security-review look, not decided or touched by this lane.

finding_not_a_defect_in_this_lane_but_wo.what: On the gold parcel, the Feasibility summary's 'Buildable area' reads 15,673 sq ft while the appended site-plan sheet's own drawn envelope label reads 15,653 SF -- a 20 sq ft (0.13%) disagreement between two numbers on the SAME document.
finding_not_a_defect_in_this_lane_but_wo.root_cause_read_from_code_not_assumed: site-model.ts: the Feasibility summary section reads summary.buildablePdfLabel, which mapBuildableDisplay() intentionally resolves from a 'warm' buildable-envelope ATOM's stored areaSqFt when one is on file (by design, so the PDF agrees with the map card elsewhere in the product). The site-plan sheet's own drawn envelope label and header stat (render.ts:551,1363-1370) read summary.buildableAreaSqFt directly -- a FRESH recomputation from the actual ring-offset polygon being drawn on that page, bypassing the warm-atom preference entirely because a drawing cannot show a number that disagrees with its own geometry.
finding_not_a_defect_in_this_lane_but_wo.why_this_is_not_a_p32_bug: Both code paths are pre-existing, unchanged by this PR. dossier.ts never surfaces this because its cover verdict line is entirely caller-supplied, never derived from summary.buildablePdfLabel. The standalone site-plan export only ever shows the ring-derived number. Feasibility is the first document in this codebase to print BOTH values on one page, which is what made a pre-existing small disagreement between a stored warm envelope atom and a fresh geometric recomputation visible for the first time.
finding_not_a_defect_in_this_lane_but_wo.relation_to_this_thread: Same class of finding as _inbox/2026-09-03_report_vocabulary_and_surface_findings.md (three declared display vocabularies; two shipped cross-surface-agreement defects in hauska-map) -- a different instance, this time inside hauska-engine itself, between a warm-atom-preferring summary label and a fresh-geometry-preferring drawing label. Named, not silently absorbed or fixed in this lane.
finding_not_a_defect_in_this_lane_but_wo.owner: unassigned -- property seat's call whether the warm-atom preference should also apply to the site-plan sheet's own label, or whether the Feasibility summary should prefer the fresh geometric value instead. Not decided or touched here.
